svg.title: CSF 2.0 and the compliance map
svg.desc: The six Functions are concurrent management areas, not six gates to finish in order. Govern spans the work; incident response also requires preparation during normal operations. Govern: Strategy, accountability, policy, risk tolerance and oversight. Identify: Inventory assets and identify and assess risks. Protect: Manage access and permissions; reduce incident likelihood and impact. Detect: Observe anomalies and produce signals that can be investigated. Respond: Determine incidents, coordinate action and limit harm. Recover: Restore important services and verify trustworthiness and availability. Laws and regulations: Fulfil duties when statutory applicability conditions are met, such as privacy law and cybersecurity law for specified entities. Standards and industry requirements: ISO/IEC 27001 for management systems and PCI DSS for payment-card data. Contracts or law can make requirements binding. Framework: NIST CSF 2.0 helps identify capabilities, objectives and gaps. Internal policy and procedures: Specify authorization, responsibility, escalation and reporting. Certification does not guarantee that incidents cannot occur.
